My Only Story - Deon Wigget v. Willem Breytenbach [5795]

By: Carol Albertyn Christie | Delivery

Proposal


Show:

Summary:
In November last year Wiggett and News24 co-published a series of podcasts called My Only Story in which Wiggett exposed Willem Breytenbach, a former Media24 executive, teacher and digital entrepreneur, as an alleged sexual predator. Breytenbach has also been accused of sexually molesting several schoolboys at three schools where he taught from 1989 to 1994, among them Grey College in Bloemfontein.

The podcasts, however, were only the tip of the iceberg. In his book, Wiggett will track Breytenbach’s trail of alleged abuse from Kroonstad, where he grew up, to Bloemfontein, the small towns of Willowmore and Riversdale, and finally to Cape Town, where he is said to have raped Wiggett and other men. Wiggett will also, for the first time, tell the full story of his own rape.

But Wiggett’s main purpose with the book is to expose the enablers of Willem Breytenbach and the system of complicity. Breytenbach, it appears, remained safe incident after incident, while his enablers covered up his alleged deeds.

‘Ever since his high-school days, people have covered up for Breytenbach,’ says Wiggett. ‘Men like him will always do what they do, but he was enabled by the teachers and executives around him, who just looked the other way for 40 years.
Since the podcast, 50 men have contacted Deon to say that they were also sexually abused by Breytenbach. Breytenbach has been arrested and is out on bail and is going to court in November.

Deon Wigget Notes


“I want him to get everything he deserves.”
That's what Deon Wiggett, the man behind SA's most talked about podcast, My Only Story, said his wish was for Willem Breytenbach.
Wiggett has accused the former teacher and Media24 executive of raping him in 1997, when he was a teenager.
The four-episode podcast was launched on November 7 and billed as a live investigation. At first, Wiggett only referred to his alleged rapist as “Jimmy”, detailing how the death of his father two years ago brought back memories of how he had allegedly been “raped in the mouth” as a teenager by a former teacher.
My Only Story has been the number-one podcast in SA since mid-November.
Police confirmed to TimesLIVE that three criminal cases and one inquiry docket had been opened since the release of My Only Story. Breytenbach was arrested on Tuesday in Hartenbos.
On Wednesday Breytenbach's lawyer, JC de Jager, confirmed to TimesLIVE Breytenbach was still in custody. He would not confirm if he would be denying the allegations or not, only saying it was a "sensitive" matter.
Exposing Breytenbach
“In the weeks leading up to episode one, I was extremely troubled about consciously ruining a man's life. But if I didn’t, he would still be free.”

Former media executive arrested for alleged sexual abuse
Former media bigshot and alleged rapist Willem Breytenbach was arrested at his psychologist's practice in Mossel Bay, in the Western Cape, on Tuesday.
NEWS
10 months ago

In the final episode of season one, Wiggett said he did the podcast for four reasons: justice, activism, art and revenge. Speaking to TimesLIVE two days after the release of that episode, he said he felt he had a responsibility to “expose Breytenbach.”
“I felt I had to do something to stop him and stop this incredible decade-long injustice from carrying on. I feel like I had the responsibility to do something because I have the means and the drive to stand up. I blame my mother entirely. My parents raised us to be deeply moral and deeply ethical — if you see an injustice, you are the one who should do something about the injustice.”
Creating conversations about male rape
“Why did I do it so publicly? Well, now we are all talking about it.”
Referring to the 16 days of activism against gender-based violence in SA, Wiggett said he believed there was an “underreported aspect” to the violence.
“I don’t believe male rape is different from female rape in what it does to the victim. Somehow there’s this idea that we need to talk about it separately and I don’t want to talk about it separately. Men are also raped.”
Wiggett said the podcast had sparked conversations about male rape, allowing debate on what he said were “uneducated questions and answers”.
“Are you going to ask me the difference between oral rape, rape and molestations? Because people ask me the question. I was raped in the mouth and I've been told I should say it was oral rape. All of these acts are personal and spiritual violence, and by having these tiers of sexual offences we’re not helping anyone.”
Overcoming fears
“If you have been raped you start thinking: 'What kind of a person would allow someone to do that to them? ... In some way it "must've been my fault".'"
In the podcast, Wiggett describes how he found out where Breytenbach lived and drove past his house. He said it was “one of the most intense things of the whole process”.
“I was so scared of him still. It was as if he was going to burst out the house and start raping and assaulting you. It's so irrational.”

Getting rid of that fear was not something that happened overnight, with Wiggett saying he only lost his fear after the first episode was released.
He highlighted the importance of seeking professional help.
“I can barely adequately express how important it is to see a psychologist if you have been a victim of rape. Or even if you haven't for that matter. I believe everyone should be in therapy.”
Layers of complicity
“It's part of the reason I worked with News24. I can't have those conversations [with the enablers].”
In the final episode of My Only Story, Wiggett spoke about the layers of complicity of those who were involved in what he called “turning a blind eye” to what Breytenbach allegedly did.
Breytenbach was a former media executive at Media24. News24, which is owned by Media24, is the media partner to the podcast. In a statement to News24, Media24 said it was “shocked” at the allegations of sex crimes against one of its senior managers.
Responding to questions by News24, former CEO Esmaré Weideman said there had been no record of complaints “of this nature” against Breytenbach and insisted all the “usual” checks had been done when the company hired Breytenbach.
Wiggett said there had been many “enablers” around Breytenbach.
“I had to quit my job and tell journalists something they've all known.”
Season two in the making?
“I have found a different way of reporting on sexual offences and sexual predators.”
Wiggett said that while he had exposed his alleged perpetrator, there were still many Jimmys out there. He said he was hoping to find funding to continue with season two of his podcast.
“Jimmy was my Jimmy, but lots of people have a Jimmy. I know of an armful of Jimmys teaching at schools in SA, having access to children in SA. Maybe we can find a different way to investigate historical sexual offences in SA.”

Probe sexual violence in Catholic church, say SA women priests
Women priests want the Roman Catholic Church to be scrutinised as the uprising against gender violence gathers momentum
NEWS
1 year ago

Finding solace
“With the help of the other survivors we have managed to stop him.”
In the final episode, Wiggett gave a moving account of how he stood outside Cape Town airport and looked at Table Mountain without being afraid. He said he had managed to find “meaning” through the creation of the podcast and thanked the other men who had been brave enough to come forward with their stories.
“To see the way these men change because they are confronting their demons has been incredible. I have met most incredible men on this journey. The resilience of these men has been the most beautiful thing to behold.”
For Wiggett it was a full-circle moment when Breytenbach closed his business and retreated to his mother's house near Hartenbos.
“More than anything I am elated about what has happened to the life of Willem Breytenbach. His departure from Cape Town has made the city an infinitely safer place and I don’t feel the compulsion any more of having to warn people the whole time.”

Deon Wigget Script


V/O
This is the remarkable story of a 40 year old man who hunted down an alleged paedophile, who he claims sexualy assaulted as a 17 year old schoolboy.

Up Sound News24

“Mr Breytenbach do you want to say anything?”

Podcast
“There is something I witnessed the year I left high school. It’s been more than 20 years now since I promised myself to forget it forever. And in many ways I did forget until now. I am Deon Wigget and this is My Only Story.”

V/O
Wigget took a year to hunt down his alleged sexual predator Willem Breytenbach, a 55 year old teacher and media executive which lead to his arrested in Reebok in December last year.

Up Sound News 24
“Mr Breyetbach do you want to say anything?”

V/O
Deon Wigget is an award winning copywriter in Johannesburg. His podcast ,
My Only Story, The Hunt for a Serial Paedophile has enthralled audiences and it became one of the most downloaded podcasts in South Africa.

Up Sound
“But memories are also chain reactions, one thought leads to another, its like you can’t rember one thing without remembering something else first.”

V/O
The story begins with the death of his father three years ago. This was the catalyst that revived a trauma he was trying so hard to forget.

Up Sound
‘If my father’s death was a seismic blow it was the weeks and months of aftershocks as the bottom fell out my life and my youth.”

Masa
“Deon what was it about your father’s passing that triggered the memories?”

Deon
If you asked me in 2016 whether I had ever met a paedophile I would have said no not to my knowledge, its sometimes called dissociative traumatic amnesia.”


Deon
“And I suddenly wondered what Willem Breytenbach has been up to.”

V/O
Wigget worked on his school newspaper in Stellenbosch and Breytenbach, who was employed at the Burger Newspaper, came to his school to encourage young journalists.

Podcast
“He is attentive and smart and lets me in on newspaper secrets and takes me under his wing. Willem Breytenbach became my hero.”

V/O
Unbeknownst to him, he claims Breytenbach had a seduction plan and invited Wigget to come and look at old newspapers at his flat one morning and then found that he was being shown pornographic photos.

Deon
“The last picture he passed to me he ran his fingers down my hand as he was taking the picture for me and I froze. It was a considerable realisation for me when I acknowledged my abuse that fight or flight is only two thirds of the equations, flight fright and freeze is really what it is. You think that it is your fault that this very large journalist is having sex with you as a matric boy and the shame of having had sex with him, I just lay there the whole time and I effectively remained frozen until the beginning of 2018 when my father died.”

Link
This unassuming loft is Wigget’s control centre it is from here that through social media he was able to find and track down the digital footprint of the man who sexually assaulted him

V/O
Wigget started an extensive search and followed the crumbs of evidence he had let behind.

He found Breytenbach on social media, usually posing with a bevy of young men.
But it was not an easy journey for Wigget.

Deon
‘In the beginning the process was terrifically hard for me, just seeing his picture, freaked me out and made me feel all of those same experiences all over again.”

Podcast
“Today he is in his 50s and lives in a picture pretty Cape Town neighbourhood, with views of Table Mountain and the Atlantic Ocean.
There’s plenty he has done in the 20 years since he has been a teacher. But we will get there.”





Masa Revoice in Mix
“The alleged perpetrator is out there living their best life, how did you deal with that injustice?”

Deon
“I made a podcast, because I realised early on if I go to the police on my own and say this happened to me, it would be my word against his, because these people operate in patterns I knew that I had to find boys that went through similar experiences, so that a critical mass of us, say the same happened to me too.”

Podcast
But what matters more to me right now is what he said to me in the 90’s, that he used to teach at one of South Africa’s most famous schools.”

Link
“Deon’s investigation lead him to Grey College, which is one of South Africa’s most prestigious high schools. It is well known for the many Springboks it has produced as well as excellent academic results.”

V/O
Deon went undercover to Bloemfontein and in their library found school photos that Breytenbach was in. He then set about tracing boys who knew him.

Podcast
“For months Grey College looked to me like Fortress Grey but now cracks are appearing , one of the men from Grey College has responded to my message , one of the boys I tracked down from a year book picture.”

V/O
A boy, Wigget calls “Ben”, to protect his identity, remembers him. Initially Breytenbach’s name was changed to “Jimmy” in the podcast, as Wigget saught corroborating evidence before naming him.

Podcast
“On the bitterly cold night that Ben is telling me about, it’s the night that Ben walked into Jimmy’s room and caught him in bed with a 15 year old class mate.”

Masa
“When you met some of these survivors, how did you feel?”

Deon
“The first survivor I met of Breytenbach is a guy called Ben and then to find this one guy who is saying me too, transformed the experience for me, because I knew at that moment that the hypothesis does hold I am on to something I just need to keep on searching.”

V/O
Ben wasn’t the only one at Grey College. Breytenbach also alledgedly had his way with a boy called Joshua.

Masa
“Who do you blame?”

Deon
‘I blame Willem Breytenbach. He is the one to whom the shame goes. That being said, there have been many opportunities over the years for Breytenbach to be stopped in his tracks. On the 10th of August 1990, he molested a boy in his room at Grey College, this boy phoned his mother the next morning and she got in her car with her husband, she told the school what happened and the school insisted it would never happen again, they will deal with this they will make a plan.”

Link
“We contacted Grey College and the current head master responded with this written statement, saying he was appointed in 2013 and had no knowledge of what happened at the school 30 years ago.

V/O
We suggested to the school that because Breytenbach was not investigated at the time, he was able to have access to other boys which he abused. The school responded.
“If this is indeed the case, it is truly a shame and a crime. Grey College Secondary condemns all forms of sexual harassment, abuse and brutality against people,especially women and children… The school will cooperate fully to see justice served.

Link
After Breytenbach’s sudden departure from Grey College he then got another teaching job at Willowmore High School where he would be exposed to even more boys.

V/O
He only stayed there for 2 years before he moved on to
Langenhoven High School in Riversdale where he was appointed the Hostel Father. That is where Hendry Freeman was allegedly sexually molested by him.We offered the school a right of reply but they suggested we contact the Department of Education.

Masa
“If you could please just take us back to the day that you first heard Deon’s podcast,?”

Hendry
“I drew the line, I opened my news app and was newsman and previously teacher and I just knew it, that is when it hit me.”



V/O
Like Wigget, Freeman also worked on his school’s news paper and was befriended by Breytenbach. He was invited to watch a movie very early one morning in his teacher’s bedroom, when Breytenbach allegedly molested him.

Masa
“Did you tell anyone that this happened to you?

Hendry
“Not at the time no. I was scared. Why would a standard 9, 17 year old boy be so stupid to go and find himself there. Why did I let myself go there?
But it happened , who should I have told, I could have gone to the school, I don’t know, my parents, what would my Dad have done?”

V/O
News24 co published Wigget’s podcast in November last year it and it quickly gained traction.

Up Sound Hello Willem….thank you bye

Podcast
“It is Sunday 17 November 2019 and I land in Cape Town, I am here to meet two more survivors of Willem and to lay charges for offences against him in 1997.”

Deon
“By selectively searching for a year I could find more than 50 survivors,are saying we are coming for you Willem Breytenbach. “

V/O
Willem Breytenbach was arrested on the 5th of December 2019, he is out on bail and he is due back in court later this month. Breytenbach’s lawyer politely declined our request for an interview.

Wigget has written a book about his quest for justice also titled My Only Story.

Masa
“How do you feel now that you have seen him arrested and in hand cuffs?”

Hendry
“I think I can now live in peace that I know now that he has now stopped, there wont be any more victims ever again.”

Podcast
‘He wont be bothering us anymore and I find peace in that.





Deon
“Now that I have faced my demons and hit back and taken back the power that was never his to take. It is really liberating to at the age of 40 get to be the Deon Wigget I have always wanted to be.”

Back references from Insert in Show: Title Author Last Updated 01 November 2020 - Carte Blanche HD nombuso@carteblanche.co.za 11 December 2020 TX Date: 0000-00-00 Script: Deon Wigget Script V/O This is the remarkable story of a 40 year old man who hunted down an alleged paedophile, who he claims sexualy assaulted as a 17 year old schoolboy. Up Sound News24 “Mr Breytenbach do you want to say anything?” Podcast “There is something I witnessed the year I left high school. It’s been more than 20 years now since I promised myself to forget it forever. And in many ways I did forget until now. I am Deon Wigget and this is My Only Story.” V/O Wigget took a year to hunt down his alleged sexual predator Willem Breytenbach, a 55 year old teacher and media executive which lead to his arrested in Reebok in December last year. Up Sound News 24 “Mr Breyetbach do you want to say anything?” V/O Deon Wigget is an award winning copywriter in Johannesburg. His podcast , My Only Story, The Hunt for a Serial Paedophile has enthralled audiences and it became one of the most downloaded podcasts in South Africa. Up Sound “But memories are also chain reactions, one thought leads to another, its like you can’t rember one thing without remembering something else first.” V/O The story begins with the death of his father three years ago. This was the catalyst that revived a trauma he was trying so hard to forget. Up Sound ‘If my father’s death was a seismic blow it was the weeks and months of aftershocks as the bottom fell out my life and my youth.” Masa “Deon what was it about your father’s passing that triggered the memories?” Deon If you asked me in 2016 whether I had ever met a paedophile I would have said no not to my knowledge, its sometimes called dissociative traumatic amnesia.” Deon “And I suddenly wondered what Willem Breytenbach has been up to.” V/O Wigget worked on his school newspaper in Stellenbosch and Breytenbach, who was employed at the Burger Newspaper, came to his school to encourage young journalists. Podcast “He is attentive and smart and lets me in on newspaper secrets and takes me under his wing. Willem Breytenbach became my hero.” V/O Unbeknownst to him, he claims Breytenbach had a seduction plan and invited Wigget to come and look at old newspapers at his flat one morning and then found that he was being shown pornographic photos. Deon “The last picture he passed to me he ran his fingers down my hand as he was taking the picture for me and I froze. It was a considerable realisation for me when I acknowledged my abuse that fight or flight is only two thirds of the equations, flight fright and freeze is really what it is. You think that it is your fault that this very large journalist is having sex with you as a matric boy and the shame of having had sex with him, I just lay there the whole time and I effectively remained frozen until the beginning of 2018 when my father died.” Link This unassuming loft is Wigget’s control centre it is from here that through social media he was able to find and track down the digital footprint of the man who sexually assaulted him V/O Wigget started an extensive search and followed the crumbs of evidence he had let behind. He found Breytenbach on social media, usually posing with a bevy of young men. But it was not an easy journey for Wigget. Deon ‘In the beginning the process was terrifically hard for me, just seeing his picture, freaked me out and made me feel all of those same experiences all over again.” Podcast “Today he is in his 50s and lives in a picture pretty Cape Town neighbourhood, with views of Table Mountain and the Atlantic Ocean. There’s plenty he has done in the 20 years since he has been a teacher. But we will get there.” Masa Revoice in Mix “The alleged perpetrator is out there living their best life, how did you deal with that injustice?” Deon “I made a podcast, because I realised early on if I go to the police on my own and say this happened to me, it would be my word against his, because these people operate in patterns I knew that I had to find boys that went through similar experiences, so that a critical mass of us, say the same happened to me too.” Podcast But what matters more to me right now is what he said to me in the 90’s, that he used to teach at one of South Africa’s most famous schools.” Link “Deon’s investigation lead him to Grey College, which is one of South Africa’s most prestigious high schools. It is well known for the many Springboks it has produced as well as excellent academic results.” V/O Deon went undercover to Bloemfontein and in their library found school photos that Breytenbach was in. He then set about tracing boys who knew him. Podcast “For months Grey College looked to me like Fortress Grey but now cracks are appearing , one of the men from Grey College has responded to my message , one of the boys I tracked down from a year book picture.” V/O A boy, Wigget calls “Ben”, to protect his identity, remembers him. Initially Breytenbach’s name was changed to “Jimmy” in the podcast, as Wigget saught corroborating evidence before naming him. Podcast “On the bitterly cold night that Ben is telling me about, it’s the night that Ben walked into Jimmy’s room and caught him in bed with a 15 year old class mate.” Masa “When you met some of these survivors, how did you feel?” Deon “The first survivor I met of Breytenbach is a guy called Ben and then to find this one guy who is saying me too, transformed the experience for me, because I knew at that moment that the hypothesis does hold I am on to something I just need to keep on searching.” V/O Ben wasn’t the only one at Grey College. Breytenbach also alledgedly had his way with a boy called Joshua. Masa “Who do you blame?” Deon ‘I blame Willem Breytenbach. He is the one to whom the shame goes. That being said, there have been many opportunities over the years for Breytenbach to be stopped in his tracks. On the 10th of August 1990, he molested a boy in his room at Grey College, this boy phoned his mother the next morning and she got in her car with her husband, she told the school what happened and the school insisted it would never happen again, they will deal with this they will make a plan.” Link “We contacted Grey College and the current head master responded with this written statement, saying he was appointed in 2013 and had no knowledge of what happened at the school 30 years ago. V/O We suggested to the school that because Breytenbach was not investigated at the time, he was able to have access to other boys which he abused. The school responded. “If this is indeed the case, it is truly a shame and a crime. Grey College Secondary condemns all forms of sexual harassment, abuse and brutality against people,especially women and children… The school will cooperate fully to see justice served. Link After Breytenbach’s sudden departure from Grey College he then got another teaching job at Willowmore High School where he would be exposed to even more boys. V/O He only stayed there for 2 years before he moved on to Langenhoven High School in Riversdale where he was appointed the Hostel Father. That is where Hendry Freeman was allegedly sexually molested by him.We offered the school a right of reply but they suggested we contact the Department of Education. Masa “If you could please just take us back to the day that you first heard Deon’s podcast,?” Hendry “I drew the line, I opened my news app and was newsman and previously teacher and I just knew it, that is when it hit me.” V/O Like Wigget, Freeman also worked on his school’s news paper and was befriended by Breytenbach. He was invited to watch a movie very early one morning in his teacher’s bedroom, when Breytenbach allegedly molested him. Masa “Did you tell anyone that this happened to you? Hendry “Not at the time no. I was scared. Why would a standard 9, 17 year old boy be so stupid to go and find himself there. Why did I let myself go there? But it happened , who should I have told, I could have gone to the school, I don’t know, my parents, what would my Dad have done?” V/O News24 co published Wigget’s podcast in November last year it and it quickly gained traction. Up Sound Hello Willem….thank you bye Podcast “It is Sunday 17 November 2019 and I land in Cape Town, I am here to meet two more survivors of Willem and to lay charges for offences against him in 1997.” Deon “By selectively searching for a year I could find more than 50 survivors,are saying we are coming for you Willem Breytenbach. “ V/O Willem Breytenbach was arrested on the 5th of December 2019, he is out on bail and he is due back in court later this month. Breytenbach’s lawyer politely declined our request for an interview. Wigget has written a book about his quest for justice also titled My Only Story. Masa “How do you feel now that you have seen him arrested and in hand cuffs?” Hendry “I think I can now live in peace that I know now that he has now stopped, there wont be any more victims ever again.” Podcast ‘He wont be bothering us anymore and I find peace in that. Deon “Now that I have faced my demons and hit back and taken back the power that was never his to take. It is really liberating to at the age of 40 get to be the Deon Wigget I have always wanted to be.” Very fast reads Promo 1 Deon Wigget suppressed the memory for over 20 years but the death of his father, was the catalyst which initiated a hunt to find the alleged serial paedophile teacher who he claims sexually assaulted him as a schoolboy. Promo 2 My Only Story is one of the most downloaded local podcasts. It tracks Deon Wigget’s hunt to find the teacher and media executive who allegedly sexually assaulted him as a school boy over 20 years ago. Promo 3 Copywriter Deon Wigget tracked down an alleged serial paedophile teacher who he claims sexually assaulted him as a schoolboy over 20 years ago, culminating in his arrest and court appearance.

metadata.Summary: In November last year Wiggett and News24 co-published a series of podcasts called My Only Story in which Wiggett exposed Willem Breytenbach, a former Media24 executive, teacher and digital entrepreneur, as an alleged sexual predator. Breytenbach has also been accused of sexually molesting several schoolboys at three schools where he taught from 1989 to 1994, among them Grey College in Bloemfontein. The podcasts, however, were only the tip of the iceberg. In his book, Wiggett will track Breytenbach’s trail of alleged abuse from Kroonstad, where he grew up, to Bloemfontein, the small towns of Willowmore and Riversdale, and finally to Cape Town, where he is said to have raped Wiggett and other men. Wiggett will also, for the first time, tell the full story of his own rape. But Wiggett’s main purpose with the book is to expose the enablers of Willem Breytenbach and the system of complicity. Breytenbach, it appears, remained safe incident after incident, while his enablers covered up his alleged deeds. ‘Ever since his high-school days, people have covered up for Breytenbach,’ says Wiggett. ‘Men like him will always do what they do, but he was enabled by the teachers and executives around him, who just looked the other way for 40 years. Since the podcast, 50 men have contacted Deon to say that they were also sexually abused by Breytenbach. Breytenbach has been arrested and is out on bail and is going to court in November.

We also have News24 footage of Breytenbach being arrested, in court etc. Courthouse Timeline Deon Wigget Notes “I want him to get everything he deserves.” That's what Deon Wiggett, the man behind SA's most talked about podcast, My Only Story, said his wish was for Willem Breytenbach. Wiggett has accused the former teacher and Media24 executive of raping him in 1997, when he was a teenager. The four-episode podcast was launched on November 7 and billed as a live investigation. At first, Wiggett only referred to his alleged rapist as “Jimmy”, detailing how the death of his father two years ago brought back memories of how he had allegedly been “raped in the mouth” as a teenager by a former teacher. My Only Story has been the number-one podcast in SA since mid-November. Police confirmed to TimesLIVE that three criminal cases and one inquiry docket had been opened since the release of My Only Story. Breytenbach was arrested on Tuesday in Hartenbos. On Wednesday Breytenbach's lawyer, JC de Jager, confirmed to TimesLIVE Breytenbach was still in custody. He would not confirm if he would be denying the allegations or not, only saying it was a "sensitive" matter. Exposing Breytenbach “In the weeks leading up to episode one, I was extremely troubled about consciously ruining a man's life. But if I didn’t, he would still be free.” Former media executive arrested for alleged sexual abuse Former media bigshot and alleged rapist Willem Breytenbach was arrested at his psychologist's practice in Mossel Bay, in the Western Cape, on Tuesday. NEWS 10 months ago In the final episode of season one, Wiggett said he did the podcast for four reasons: justice, activism, art and revenge. Speaking to TimesLIVE two days after the release of that episode, he said he felt he had a responsibility to “expose Breytenbach.” “I felt I had to do something to stop him and stop this incredible decade-long injustice from carrying on. I feel like I had the responsibility to do something because I have the means and the drive to stand up. I blame my mother entirely. My parents raised us to be deeply moral and deeply ethical — if you see an injustice, you are the one who should do something about the injustice.” Creating conversations about male rape “Why did I do it so publicly? Well, now we are all talking about it.” Referring to the 16 days of activism against gender-based violence in SA, Wiggett said he believed there was an “underreported aspect” to the violence. “I don’t believe male rape is different from female rape in what it does to the victim. Somehow there’s this idea that we need to talk about it separately and I don’t want to talk about it separately. Men are also raped.” Wiggett said the podcast had sparked conversations about male rape, allowing debate on what he said were “uneducated questions and answers”. “Are you going to ask me the difference between oral rape, rape and molestations? Because people ask me the question. I was raped in the mouth and I've been told I should say it was oral rape. All of these acts are personal and spiritual violence, and by having these tiers of sexual offences we’re not helping anyone.” Overcoming fears “If you have been raped you start thinking: 'What kind of a person would allow someone to do that to them? ... In some way it "must've been my fault".'" In the podcast, Wiggett describes how he found out where Breytenbach lived and drove past his house. He said it was “one of the most intense things of the whole process”. “I was so scared of him still. It was as if he was going to burst out the house and start raping and assaulting you. It's so irrational.” Getting rid of that fear was not something that happened overnight, with Wiggett saying he only lost his fear after the first episode was released. He highlighted the importance of seeking professional help. “I can barely adequately express how important it is to see a psychologist if you have been a victim of rape. Or even if you haven't for that matter. I believe everyone should be in therapy.” Layers of complicity “It's part of the reason I worked with News24. I can't have those conversations [with the enablers].” In the final episode of My Only Story, Wiggett spoke about the layers of complicity of those who were involved in what he called “turning a blind eye” to what Breytenbach allegedly did. Breytenbach was a former media executive at Media24. News24, which is owned by Media24, is the media partner to the podcast. In a statement to News24, Media24 said it was “shocked” at the allegations of sex crimes against one of its senior managers. Responding to questions by News24, former CEO Esmaré Weideman said there had been no record of complaints “of this nature” against Breytenbach and insisted all the “usual” checks had been done when the company hired Breytenbach. Wiggett said there had been many “enablers” around Breytenbach. “I had to quit my job and tell journalists something they've all known.” Season two in the making? “I have found a different way of reporting on sexual offences and sexual predators.” Wiggett said that while he had exposed his alleged perpetrator, there were still many Jimmys out there. He said he was hoping to find funding to continue with season two of his podcast. “Jimmy was my Jimmy, but lots of people have a Jimmy. I know of an armful of Jimmys teaching at schools in SA, having access to children in SA. Maybe we can find a different way to investigate historical sexual offences in SA.” Probe sexual violence in Catholic church, say SA women priests Women priests want the Roman Catholic Church to be scrutinised as the uprising against gender violence gathers momentum NEWS 1 year ago Finding solace “With the help of the other survivors we have managed to stop him.” In the final episode, Wiggett gave a moving account of how he stood outside Cape Town airport and looked at Table Mountain without being afraid. He said he had managed to find “meaning” through the creation of the podcast and thanked the other men who had been brave enough to come forward with their stories. “To see the way these men change because they are confronting their demons has been incredible. I have met most incredible men on this journey. The resilience of these men has been the most beautiful thing to behold.” For Wiggett it was a full-circle moment when Breytenbach closed his business and retreated to his mother's house near Hartenbos. “More than anything I am elated about what has happened to the life of Willem Breytenbach. His departure from Cape Town has made the city an infinitely safer place and I don’t feel the compulsion any more of having to warn people the whole time.”
